questions.question: Why do people work?
options: To earn money for daily life and fulfill their duties
questions.explanation: People work to earn money for their daily lives - food, housing, clothing, and other needs.

questions.question: Chrumko notices his mom getting ready for work in the morning. Why does she work even when it's raining?
options: So she can earn money from her work to pay for housing, food, and school supplies
questions.explanation: Mom has to go to work because she earns money from her work with which the family pays for everything they need.

questions.question: What value do people's jobs have in society?
options: They help others - they teach, heal, repair, manufacture, provide services
questions.explanation: Many people help others through their work. Every job has its value because it contributes to society functioning.

questions.question: What does Chrumko realize?
options: Work helps secure many things they have at home and are taken for granted
questions.explanation: Chrumko realizes that work helps secure many things they have at home and are taken for granted.

questions.question: Do all adults do the same work?
options: Yes, everyone does the same thing
No, people have different occupations based on their skills and abilities
questions.explanation: People have different occupations based on what they know, what they enjoy, and what society needs.

questions.question: Chrumko goes to school in the morning. How many different types of work does he see?
options: Bus driver, teacher, road workers and others in the store and post office
questions.explanation: Chrumko sees how many different people work - drivers, teachers, workers, salespeople, postal workers, and others.

questions.question: What are the types of occupations?
options: Jobs with people, technology, animals, buildings, or information
questions.explanation: There are occupations where people make something, repair, teach, heal, organize, or work with information.

questions.question: Why is it important to have different occupations?
options: All complement each other and together help the world function
questions.explanation: Each occupation has its purpose. All different jobs complement each other and together help the world function.

questions.question: Does everyone earn the same money for their work?
options: No, salary depends on the type of work, experience, and responsibility
questions.explanation: The salary amount depends on the type of work, experience, responsibility, and the time a person dedicates to work.

questions.question: How often does someone get paid for their work?
questions.explanation: A person gets paid regularly, usually once a month into their bank account.

questions.question: Chrumko talks to his father about salaries. What does his father say?
options: He gets paid once a month and the family pays for everything with that money
questions.explanation: His father explains that he gets paid once a month and the family gradually pays for everything throughout the month from that money.

questions.question: What does Chrumko understand?
options: Money from work must be wisely divided over a longer period
questions.explanation: Chrumko understands that money from work must be wisely divided so it lasts a longer time.

questions.question: Why is time important in work?
options: A person earns money based on the time they spend working
questions.explanation: In many jobs, people are paid based on the time they work - the more hours, the greater the reward.

questions.question: Chrumko sees his older brother working at the neighbors'. What is he doing?
options: Helps for the whole morning - rakes leaves, sweeps grass, carries branches
questions.explanation: His brother works over the weekend for the whole morning. They work together and spend time and effort on it.

questions.question: What does his brother get for the work?
questions.explanation: After the work, his brother gets a small reward. The neighbor explains that the reward is for the time and help he gave.

questions.question: What does Chrumko realize?
options: Time and effort are counted in work
questions.explanation: Chrumko realizes that time and effort are counted in work. More time or better work means a higher reward.

questions.question: What is productivity?
options: How much work a person can do in a certain time
questions.explanation: Productivity means how much work a person can do in a certain time. If they work focused, they do more in less time.

questions.question: Chrumko is doing his homework. On the first day, he keeps looking at his phone. What happens?
options: The homework takes a short time
The homework takes a very long time because he's distracted
questions.explanation: The homework takes a very long time because he keeps getting distracted and interrupting his work.

questions.question: On the second day, Chrumko sits differently. What is he doing?
options: He sits without interruptions, prepares everything he needs, and works focused
questions.explanation: Chrumko sits without interruptions, prepares everything, and works focused. This time he does better.

questions.question: How long does the homework take him on the second day?
questions.explanation: He finishes it faster and without stress. Chrumko realizes that when he works carefully, he accomplishes more in less time.

questions.question: What is a budget?
options: A plan that shows how much money we have and what we want to use it for
questions.explanation: A budget is a plan that shows how much money we have and what we want to use it for. It helps with money.

questions.question: Chrumko sees his mom writing numbers in a notebook. What is she doing?
options: Planning expenses for the whole month
questions.explanation: His mom is planning expenses for the whole month. First she writes the money she will receive, then what needs to be paid.

questions.question: How does his mom make a budget?
options: Write down money, expenses, then think about what's left
questions.explanation: His mom writes down the money the family will receive and then the expenses. Only then does she think about what's left.

questions.question: What is the goal of a budget?
options: So people can better divide money and avoid financial problems
questions.explanation: A budget helps you have order in your money and know how much you can afford.

questions.question: What are income and expenses?
options: Income - money coming in; Expenses - money going out
questions.explanation: Income is money coming in. Expenses is money that the household spends.

questions.question: Chrumko thinks that when his parents get paid, they can buy everything. What does his father say?
options: First you have to subtract housing, food, and other bills
questions.explanation: His father tells him that first you have to subtract housing, food, and other bills. Only then is there a smaller amount left.

questions.question: What happens if expenses are higher than income?
questions.explanation: If expenses are higher than income, money can run short and the family will have a problem.

questions.question: What does Chrumko realize?
options: What's important is not just what comes in, but also what goes out
questions.explanation: Chrumko realizes that what's important is not just what comes in, but also what goes out and what it's spent on.

questions.question: Why don't people spend all the money at the beginning of the month?
options: Because money needs to last the whole month
questions.explanation: Money often needs to last the whole month. That's why families plan what they will need now and what later.

questions.question: Chrumko suggests buying a new game right after getting paid. What does his mom say?
options: First we must pay important bills, then we can see what we can afford
questions.explanation: His mom explains that first they must pay everything important. In a few days, other bills will come.

questions.question: What does Chrumko realize?
options: Money needs to be spread over a longer time
questions.explanation: Chrumko understands that money needs to be spread over a longer time to last the whole month.

questions.question: Why is planning important?
options: It helps avoid financial problems and know when they can afford what
questions.explanation: Planning helps you know in advance what you'll spend money on and avoid unexpected problems.

questions.question: What are fixed expenses?
options: Payments that repeat regularly with a similar amount
questions.explanation: Fixed expenses are payments that repeat regularly, like rent, utilities, and insurance. They usually stay the same each month.

questions.question: What are examples of fixed expenses in a family?
options: Housing, electricity, water, food, and school supplies
questions.explanation: Fixed expenses typically include housing, electricity, water, basic food, and school supplies - things the family needs regularly.
